hints.title: 1 · Draw the transition table
hints.body: List each transport outcome, the next status, whether attempts increases, and whether to raise. A terminal record must return before calling transport.

hints.title: 2 · Commit before signaling retry
hints.body: For a fictional ImportJob: update!(attempts: attempts + 1, status: "pending"); raise Retryable. Raising inside a transaction that surrounds the update can roll back the very evidence you need to persist.

hints.title: 3 · Catch only the expected transport exception
hints.body: Rescue DeliveryTransport::Unavailable explicitly. Keep programming and database failures visible. Success clears last_error; an outage clears last_http_status. Confirm a retry uses reloaded persisted state and the third attempt stops.

criteria.title: State-machine correctness
criteria.target: All published HTTP classes and Unavailable produce the correct durable status, attempt count, and exception behavior.
criteria.probe: Walk through 503, 429, then 200. What is persisted each time?
criteria.practice: Build a transition table and convert each row into a test.

criteria.title: Duplicate and retry behavior
criteria.target: Terminal/missing jobs are no-ops, retries stop after three attempts, and successful retries clear stale errors.
criteria.probe: When can a crash still cause a duplicate remote effect?

criteria.title: Failure classification
criteria.target: Only expected transport outages are normalized; programming/storage errors remain visible.
criteria.probe: What would rescue StandardError hide here?
criteria.practice: Practice distinct handling for client, transient transport, and programming failures.

criteria.title: Operational reasoning
criteria.target: Explain scheduler responsibility, backoff, evidence retention, and the limits of sequential duplicate suppression.
criteria.probe: How would concurrent workers claim a record safely?
criteria.practice: Design a bounded retry schedule and an operator replay policy as a separate extension.

follow_up: Add durable scheduling, jittered backoff, worker claiming, a dead-letter view, and a stable downstream idempotency key. Explain crashes before and after remote acceptance. No exactly-once guarantee is implied.
